encyclopedie.consigne: Select a platform feature to audit its 3 Sharia-Compliant evidence pillars:

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah At-Tawbah, v.34: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and spend not in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
According to Amr ibn Shu'ayb (Abu Dawoud no. 1563, Authenticated), the Prophet ﷺ saw a woman with her daughter wearing two heavy gold bracelets. He said: 'Do you pay the Zakat on this?' She said: 'No'. He said: 'Would you be pleased for Allah to dress you with two bracelets of fire on account of them?'.

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
• Hanafi School: Strict taxation at 2.5% of all gold owned, the use of jewelry does not change its taxable nature.
• Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali Schools: Exemption for a woman's lawful ornamental gold. Only investment or savings gold is subject to the tax.

quiz.question: According to the Hanafi school, is gold jewelry worn by a woman subject to Zakat?
quiz.explication: The Hanafi school levies 2.5% on all gold owned: the use as jewelry does not change its taxable status.

quiz.question: Which schools exempt a woman's lawful jewelry from Zakat?
quiz.explication: Only investment or savings gold is taxed according to the Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali schools.

quiz.question: In the hadith narrated by Abu Dawoud, what was the questioned woman wearing according to the Prophet ﷺ?
quiz.explication: The Prophet ﷺ asked her if she paid Zakat on them, before the warning about the bracelets of fire.

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah Al-An'am, v.141: 'And pay the due thereof upon the day of its harvest.'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
Narrated by Jabir (Muslim no. 981), the Prophet ﷺ said: 'For that which is irrigated by rivers or rain, one-tenth (10%) is due. For that which is artificially irrigated, a half-tenth (5%) is due.' The threshold (Nisab) is set at 5 Wasaqs (approximately 653 kg).

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
Unanimous consensus on irrigation rates. Regarding livestock, the official charter of Abu Bakr (Al-Bukhari no. 1454) sets the threshold for sheep: from 40 to 120 sheep = 1 sheep due. Below 40 heads, no Zakat is required.

quiz.question: What Zakat rate applies to naturally irrigated crops (rain, groundwater)?
quiz.explication: The full tithe (10%) is due for natural irrigation; half-tithe (5%) for artificial irrigation.

quiz.question: How many sheep must one own at minimum before livestock Zakat becomes mandatory?
quiz.explication: Below 40 heads, no Zakat is due; from 40 to 120, a single sheep is due.

quiz.question: The Nisab threshold for harvests corresponds approximately to which weight?
quiz.explication: Agricultural Nisab is set at 5 Wasaqs, or roughly 653 kg.

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah An-Nissa, v.11: The distribution of shares only takes place after applying the sovereign clause: '...after payment of legacies he may have bequeathed or debts.'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
Narrated by Salamah ibn al-Akwah (Al-Bukhari no. 2289), a dead person was brought to the Prophet ﷺ for him to pray over. He asked: 'Did he leave any debts?' They said: 'Yes, three dinars'. He said: 'Pray over your companion (I will not pray over him)' until a companion guaranteed payment of his debt.

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
• Passive Debts: Absolute priority over inheritance and Wasiyya. Among Malikis and Hanbalis, they also reduce the taxable base of financial Zakat.
• Active Debts (Receivables): If recoverable (solvent debtor), the Hanafi school levies Zakat every year, while the Maliki school requires payment only once upon recovery.

quiz.question: According to the hadith of Salamah ibn al-Akwah, how many dinars did the deceased owe?
quiz.explication: The Prophet ﷺ refused to pray over him until a companion guaranteed those 3 dinars.

quiz.question: What must imperatively be settled before successoral sharing?
quiz.explication: Surah An-Nissa v.11: distribution occurs only after executing the testament and paying debts.

quiz.question: For a recoverable receivable, which school requires Zakat every year?
quiz.explication: The Maliki school requires a one-time payment upon recovery, unlike the Hanafi school.

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah An-Nissa, v.11: 'Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females.'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
Narrated by Ibn Abbas (Al-Bukhari no. 6732, Muslim no. 1615), the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Give the fixed shares (Fara'idh) to those who are entitled to them. What remains after that belongs to the closest male relative of the deceased.'

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
Absolute consensus on the double-ratio distribution. This rule is backed by the financial maintenance obligation (Nafaqah) exclusively incumbent upon the male. The woman retains the entirety of her share for her private use without any obligation to spend it on the household. Potential beneficiaries include descendants, ascendants, collaterals (brothers, sisters, full and paternal paternal uncles, nephews, cousins) and the surviving spouse.

quiz.question: According to the Quran (An-Nissa v.11), what is the son's share compared to the daughter's?
quiz.explication: "For the male, what is equal to the share of two females" — the base ratio is 2 to 1.

quiz.question: According to the hadith narrated by Ibn Abbas, to whom does the remainder go after fixed shares?
choix: To the male closest to the deceased
It is redistributed equally among all
quiz.explication: "What remains after that belongs to the closest male relative of the deceased" — this is the principle of Asabah.

quiz.question: What financial obligation justifies the 2-to-1 ratio in favor of males?
quiz.explication: The man bears the financial burden of the household; the woman keeps her share without spending obligation.

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah An-Nissa, v.12: 'And if a man or a woman is inherited left childless (Kalâlah) and has a brother or a sister, then for each of them is a sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third.'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
When asked about the exact meaning of Kalâlah, Caliph Abu Bakr As-Siddiq (Validated by the consensus of companions) said: 'Kalâlah is one who has neither direct descendant (child) nor direct male ascendant (father/grandfather).'

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
In the case of Kalâlah, uterine siblings (mother's side) inherit in strictly equal parts between males and females (the sole exception to the double ratio). Full siblings, however, receive the remainder as residual heirs (Asabah).

quiz.question: How did Caliph Abu Bakr define Kalâlah?
choix: One who has neither descendant nor direct male ascendant
One who is a paternal orphan
quiz.explication: Neither child, nor father, nor grandfather — this is the definition validated by consensus of companions.

quiz.question: In the case of Kalâlah, how is the inheritance shared among uterine brothers and sisters?
choix: Equal share between males and females
quiz.explication: This is the unique exception to the usual 2-to-1 ratio.

quiz.question: If more than two uterine brothers/sisters are involved, what fraction do they share?
quiz.explication: For two or fewer, one-sixth each; beyond that, they share one-third.

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah Al-Baqarah, v.180: 'Prescribed for you when death approaches [any] one of you if he leaves wealth [is that he should make] a bequest for the parents and near relatives according to what is acceptable...'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
Narrated by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (Al-Bukhari no. 2744, Muslim no. 1628), when he was sick and wanted to give away all his wealth in charity, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Give one-third. And one-third is much. Indeed, leaving your heirs rich is better than leaving them poor, begging from people.'

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
Unanimous consensus: Wasiyya is strictly forbidden in favor of a legal heir (unless unanimously agreed upon by other heirs after death), and it is capped at a maximum of one-third (1/3) of the net estate after clearing debts. The application automatically blocks any surplus.

quiz.question: What is the maximum limit of Wasiyya (testament) relative to the net estate?
quiz.explication: Unanimous consensus of the four schools: one-third maximum, after clearing debts.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ reply to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who wanted to give everything in charity?
choix: "Give one-third, and one-third is a lot"
quiz.explication: He added: it is better to leave your heirs rich than poor and begging.

quiz.question: Can one bequeath by testament to a legal heir already provided with a fixed share?
choix: No, unless unanimously agreed by other heirs
quiz.explication: Wasiyya in favor of a legal heir is forbidden unless unanimously validated after death.

categories.texte:
✨ PART A: QURANIC FOUNDATION
Surah Al-Hashr, v.18: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow.'

✨ PART B: AUTHENTIC HADITH
• On White Days (At-Tirmidhi no. 761, Authentic): The Prophet ﷺ said: 'If you fast three days of the month, then fast the 13th, 14th, and 15th.' Fasting these days is equivalent to fasting a lifetime.
• On supererogatory prayers (Muslim no. 728): The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever prays twelve supererogatory Rak'ahs every day, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.'

✨ PART C: FIQH OF THE FOUR SCHOOLS (SUNNI)
Consensus on the highly meritorious character (Sunnah Muakkadah) of attached prayers (Rawatib) and fasting on white days, which are essential tools for the daily purification of the soul.

quiz.question: Which days of the month correspond to the recommended "White Days" for fasting?
quiz.explication: Narrated by At-Tirmidhi: fasting these three days is equivalent to fasting a lifetime.

quiz.question: How many daily supererogatory Rak'ahs are associated with the promise of a house in Paradise?
quiz.explication: Narrated by Muslim: twelve Rawatib Rak'ahs each day.

quiz.question: Which verse of Surah Al-Hashr exhorts every soul to look at what it has prepared for tomorrow?
quiz.explication: "And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow."

etapes.source: University of Medina, Book 2, Lesson 1: Al-Fi'l al-Madi (the past tense) — see Islamic Sciences/University of Madinah/tome_2/tome_2_grammaire.pdf

temps.note_pedagogique: The future tense does not change conjugation: it simply adds a prefix before the present tense. سَـ (sa-) for a near or general future — the form shown here. سَوْفَ (sawfa), separated, for a more distant or emphatic future: سَوْفَ يَذْهَبُ (sawfa yadhhabu) has the same meaning as سَيَذْهَبُ, with an added nuance of remoteness or emphasis.

The imperative exists only for the 2nd person ("you") — one can only command directly someone being spoken to. To say "let's go" or "let him go", Arabic uses another construction (li- + jussive), which will be seen later. Here, only 5 forms, not 14: the 2nd person has no masc./fem. distinction in the dual. Another essential point: depending on the verb, the imperative hamza is not always pronounced the same — see the 3 rules below before the cards.

regles_type_verbe.regle: When the vowel of the penultimate letter in the present tense is a damma (ُ), the imperative hamza also takes a damma.
When this vowel is a fatha or a kasra, the imperative hamza takes a kasra — this is the case for our model verb dhahaba.

For hollow verbs (whose 2nd radical is wāw or yā', like nāma), this letter disappears in the jazm mode: what remains after removing the prefix can already be pronounced alone, without any supporting vowel.

temps.note_temporelle: The imperative and prohibitive have no proper past or future: by nature, an order always designates an action that has not yet taken place — the future is already contained within the very meaning of these two modes. To report an order in the past or future (indirect speech), Arabic changes construction: an ordinary verb (amara / nahā) followed by an + a verb in the mansūb (subjunctive).

exemples_temporels.sens: he ordered him to go (past reported order)
he will order him to go (future reported order)
he forbade him to go (past reported prohibition)

temps.note_pedagogique: The prohibitive ("do not do") is formed with lā + the verb in the jazm mode (jussive — same ending as the negative future). Structure: lā + present tense form with imperative ending. Unlike the Amr, the Nahy poses no hamza vowel-timbre problem: the present prefix ta- always stays in place, and lā is simply placed before it.
temps.note_temporelle: The imperative and prohibitive have no proper past or future: by nature, an order always designates an action that has not yet taken place — the future is already contained within the very meaning of these two modes. lecons.titre: 1. الكلمة وأقسامها - The Three Types of Words
lecons.explication:
Every Arabic word belongs to one of these three categories: ism (noun), fi'l (verb), or harf (particle). Recognizing which one changes everything, because each behaves differently in a sentence.

The ism (noun) can be preceded by the article al-, take the tanwīn (ـٌ ـً ـٍ), and act as a subject. The fi'l (verb) conjugates across tenses — exactly what we manipulated in the previous step with dhahaba / yadhhabu / sayadhhabu. The harf (particle) only takes on meaning when attached to a noun or verb: on its own, it means nothing.

exemples.sens: a book (ism — accepts al- and tanwīn)
in (harf — only has meaning with a word after it)

lecons.explication:
The nominal sentence is built in two blocks: the mubtada' (subject being discussed, almost always definite) and the khabar (what is said about it, the new information). Both normally take the marfū' case (nominative), recognizable by the damma ـُ or the tanwīn ـٌ.

In "Al-baytu jamīlun" (the house is beautiful): al-baytu is the mubtada' — made definite by al-, so we already know what we are talking about. Jamīlun is the khabar — indefinite, marked with tanwīn, it is the new information we are bringing.

Most feminine nouns and adjectives are recognized by the final ة (tā' marbūta), pronounced like a light "a" in pause. Adding this letter to a masculine word generally feminizes it.

Exceptions to know: some words are feminine by nature, without any written mark — they behave as feminine in agreement even though nothing signals it to the eye.

exemples.sens: a male student / a female student
mother (feminine without ة — exception to memorize)

lecons.titre: 4. المفرد والمثنى والجمع - Singular, Dual, Plural
lecons.explication:
Arabic distinguishes three numbers, not two: mufrad (just one), muthannā (exactly two, with its own ending ـَانِ), and jam' (three or more).

The plural is formed in two ways: jam' sālim ("sound plural", regular, you add a predictable ending), or jam' taksīr ("broken plural", the word changes its internal form, to be learned case by case — this is the most common case for everyday nouns).

exemples.sens: books (jam' taksīr — the form changes entirely)

lecons.explication:
An-nakirah (indefinite) designates an unspecified thing, usually marked by tanwīn: "rajulun" means "a man", any man.

Al-ma'rifah (definite) has several forms: the noun preceded by al- ("ar-rajulu", this specific man), proper nouns (already definite by nature, even with tanwīn), pronouns (huwa, anta, anā...) and demonstratives (hādhā, hādhihi...) — all designate something specific without needing al-.

exemples.sens: the man, this man (ma'rifah — definite by al-)

lecons.explication: An ism jāmid is a "base" noun, which is not derived from a verb: it is a simple word, with no direct morphological link to a verbal root. Most concrete everyday nouns belong to this category.

An ism mushtaqq is manufactured from a verbal root: it carries the meaning of the action. The two most useful derivatives to know:

Ism al-fā'il (active participle): "he who does...". Ism al-maf'ūl (passive participle): "that which undergoes... / that which has been done". These two derivatives are built directly from the verb forms of the following section (Al-Awzān) — the bridge between them is direct.

exemples.sens: a writer, the one who writes (ism al-fā'il, from
